name: Baseball
guide: Use one batting sheet per team. Record every plate appearance, advance runners on the diamond, mark outs and shade completed runs. Use a continuation sheet for batting around or extra innings. Sum runs by inning; hits and errors are separate totals.

name: Slo-Pitch Softball
guide: Use one batting sheet per team. Maintain the agreed batting order, including extra hitters. Track each plate appearance and runner advancement. Enter league run caps, home-run limits, courtesy-runner and tie-break rules before play; local rules vary.

name: Ice Hockey
guide: Enter goals chronologically with period, clock time, scorer and up to two credited assists. Record penalties separately, including duration and release time. Keep shootout attempts separate from regulation and overtime goals; apply the competition's final-score convention.

name: Soccer
guide: Record each goal and its minute, including stoppage time (for example 45+2). Mark own goals and penalty goals. Record cautions, send-offs and substitutions separately. Keep penalty-shootout results separate from the match goal total.

name: Cornhole
guide: Each side throws four bags per round. Hole = 3; on board = 1; other bags = 0. Subtract the lower raw total from the higher: only that side scores the difference. Equal totals score zero. Finish the round; first to 21 or more wins. No exact-21 or bust rule in this format.

name: Box Lacrosse
guide: Record goals, credited assists, penalties and goalkeeper totals. This sheet uses four quarters for World Lacrosse box play. Some domestic box competitions use three periods: relabel the period columns and enter your local format before play.

name: Field Lacrosse
guide: Record goals chronologically with quarter and clock time. Credit assists only when awarded under the competition's scoring rules. Record penalties or cards, goalkeeper saves and overtime separately. Specify men's or women's field rules and period lengths before play.

name: Basketball
guide: For standard 5-on-5 basketball, a free throw is 1 point, a field goal inside the arc is 2 and beyond the arc is 3. Record each scoring event and the updated score. Track player fouls and timeouts; apply your league's period lengths and foul limits. Not a 3x3 sheet.

name: Indoor Volleyball
guide: Rally scoring: every rally awards a point. Standard indoor matches are best of five sets; sets 1-4 go to 25 and set 5 to 15, always win by two. Record the actual final points and set winner; do not add points across sets to determine the match winner. Note local format changes.

name: Pickleball - Side-Out
guide: Traditional side-out scoring awards points only to the serving side. Typical games go to 11, win by two; enter your event's target. In doubles call server score, receiver score, server number. The opening service turn starts 0-0-2. Track server changes and side-outs in the rally log.

name: Tennis
guide: Standard advantage games use love, 15, 30, 40, deuce and advantage; win by two points. A standard tie-break set is first to six games by two, with a tie-break at 6-6. Record set games and tie-break points separately. Enter no-ad or deciding match tie-break rules before play.

name: American Football
guide: Record each scoring play: touchdown 6, field goal 3, safety 2; a try is 1 or 2 under the applicable rules. Record the try separately from the touchdown. Sum each quarter and overtime into the final score. This is an American-football sheet; Canadian singles are not included.

name: Golf - Stroke Play
guide: Enter gross strokes on every hole, including penalty strokes. Total front nine (OUT) and back nine (IN), then add for gross total. Keep handicap deductions and net scores separate. Player and marker check and certify the hole scores. This sheet is for stroke play, not Stableford or match play.
